posts.title: Best Mechanical Keyboards Under $100
posts.excerpt: Looking for a quality mechanical keyboard without breaking the bank? We've tested dozens of options to bring you the best keyboards under $100.
posts.summary: Our picks for the best mechanical keyboards under $100 include the Keychron K8, Royal Kludge RK84, and Akko 3098B. These boards offer hot-swap, wireless connectivity, and excellent build quality at accessible prices.
posts.content:
## Why Buy a Mechanical Keyboard Under $100?

You don't need to spend $200+ to get an excellent typing experience. The sub-$100 market has exploded with quality options featuring premium build, hot-swap sockets, wireless connectivity, and satisfying acoustics.

## Our Top Picks

After testing dozens of keyboards, here are our recommendations for different needs and preferences. Each has been used extensively for typing, gaming, and everyday work.

### Best Overall: Keychron K8

The Keychron K8 offers the best balance of features, build quality, and price. With wireless connectivity, hot-swap option, and Mac-first design, it's perfect for most users.

### Best Budget: Royal Kludge RK61

At under $50, the RK61 is unbeatable value. Hot-swap, triple-mode wireless, and compact 60% form factor make it ideal for beginners.
keyTakeaways: Hot-swappable boards let you customize switches without soldering
Wireless options like Keychron K8 offer great flexibility
Gasket-mounted boards under $100 provide premium sound and feel
PBT keycaps are worth prioritizing for durability
65% and 75% layouts offer the best balance of compactness and functionality

faqs.question: Is a mechanical keyboard worth it under $100?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many sub-$100 mechanical keyboards now offer features previously only found in premium boards.

faqs.question: What switches should I choose?
faqs.answer: For beginners, try tactile (Brown) or linear (Red/Yellow) switches. Avoid clicky in shared spaces.

posts.title: Beginner's Guide to Mechanical Keyboards
posts.excerpt: New to mechanical keyboards? This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know.
posts.summary: Everything a beginner needs to know about mechanical keyboards, from switches to layouts.
posts.content:
## What is a Mechanical Keyboard?

Unlike membrane keyboards, mechanical keyboards use individual switches for each key.

## Switch Types

- **Linear**: Smooth keystroke, no bump
- **Tactile**: Bump feedback without click
- **Clicky**: Audible click with tactile bump

## Keyboard Sizes

- Full-size (100%)
- TKL (80%)
- 75%
- 65%
- 60%
keyTakeaways: Mechanical keyboards use individual switches per key
Three main switch types: linear, tactile, clicky
Size depends on your desk space and needs

faqs.question: Are mechanical keyboards louder?
faqs.answer: It depends on the switch type. Linear switches can be very quiet.

posts.title: Switch Types Explained
posts.excerpt: Learn the differences between linear, tactile, and clicky switches.
posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to mechanical keyboard switch types.
posts.content:
## Linear Switches

Smooth from top to bottom. Popular: Cherry MX Red, Gateron Yellow.

## Tactile Switches

Bump feedback without click. Popular: Cherry MX Brown, Zealios V2.

## Clicky Switches

Audible click with tactile bump. Popular: Cherry MX Blue, Box Jade.
keyTakeaways: Linear for gaming and quiet environments

faqs.question: Which switch is best for typing?
faqs.answer: Tactile switches provide the best typing feedback for most people.

posts.title: PBT vs ABS Keycaps
posts.excerpt: Understanding keycap materials and when to choose each.
posts.summary: A comparison of PBT and ABS keycap materials.
posts.content:
## PBT Keycaps

Durable, textured, resistant to shine. More expensive.

## ABS Keycaps

Smooth, vibrant colors, develops shine. More affordable.

faqs.question: Do PBT keycaps feel different?
faqs.answer: Yes, they typically have a more textured, matte feel.
